sentences.text: Satya Surya Phani Kumar Akella vs The State Of Telangana And

Another on 14 August, 2024
 1
The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal

Criminal Petition No.6051 Of 2019
Order:

The present Criminal Petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused in C.C.No.31 of 2017 on the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad (for short, "the trial Court") for the offences punishable under Sections 379,
468, 471 and 420 of I.P.C.
2.

Heard Mr.G.Sundareshan, learned counsel for the petitioner, Ms.S.Madhavi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1-State and Mr.G.Ravi Mohan, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that on 24.07.2015, respondent No.2 received SMS from Standard Chartered Bank vide S.C.Card No.4622 7354 5012 0648 stating that a fraudulent transaction was done with his credit card.

Respondent No.2 noticed that some unknown culprits had committed theft of his wallet and that the Citi bank card No.4386 2805 2381 6794, Voter ID Card and his pass port size photographs were also stolen by some unknown culprits and that several money transactions were also made, with respect to the card, within a span of five minutes.
On enquiry, it was found that the said transactions were made at Kamakshi Service Centre, Nizamabad.
Basing on the said facts, Crime No.660 of 2015 was registered against the petitioner for the offences under Sections 379, 468, 471 and 420 of I.P.C.
The said crime was taken cognizance of and numbered as C.C.No.31 of 2017 before the trial Court.
Hence, the present Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner, seeking to quash the impugned proceedings.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that without conducting proper investigation, the present complaint is registered against the petitioner and when the case came up for hearing before the trial Court, the petitioner was in jail, at Mumbai.
Therefore, the petitioner could not attend the trial Court, due to which, NBWs were issued against the petitioner.
He further stated that the petitioner does not possess any dishonest intention and if investigated further, the said allegations would not withstand the scrutiny of law.

To substantiate his contention, learned counsel relied upon the decisions passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vishal Noble Singh V. State of Uttar Pradesh and another 1, Criminal Appeal No.1592 of 2023 (@ SLP (CRL.) No.6688 of 2017) 2 and Criminal Appeal No.749 of 2022 dated 10.05.2022 3 and seeks to quash the impugned proceedings.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that unless and until a full-fledged trial is conducted, the truth cannot be elicited.
Therefore, she seeks to dismiss the Criminal Petition.
6. This Court vide order dated 20.11.2019 granted interim stay of impugned proceedings against the petitioner and the said order was extended from time to time.

7. Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel, this Court is of the opinion that the matter requires adjudication at length and only upon conclusion of a full-fledged trial, the truth would come to light.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to entertain the Criminal Petition at the premature stage and the Criminal Petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is dismissed.

However, the appearance of the petitioner,
before the trial Court, is dispensed with on all occasions, unless and until required.
Criminal Appeal (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.2389 of 2023) 2023 Live Law (SC) 446 3 2022 Live Law (SC) 468 Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
